evals.name: scan-updates
evals.prompt: Can you check if any of my globally installed Claude Code skills or plugins are out of date? I want to know what has updates available.
evals.expected_output: A categorized report of installed plugins AND standalone skills showing which have newer versions available at their source (compared against fetched remote latest), which are current, and which can't be determined; read-only; points the user to /plugin and the skills installer to apply updates.
assertions: Enumerates real installed plugins by name
Compares against source's latest (fetched), not a stale local copy; no false positives on current plugins
Correctly flags genuinely out-of-date plugins as having updates
Covers standalone skills tracked in ~/.agents/.skill-lock.json: clones their source repos, diffs installed folders, and reports skill updates and removed-upstream skills

Does not report a false update when an installed record's version is current but its recorded sha is stale (resolves the installed version against upstream tags / the manifest pin instead of trusting the recorded sha blindly)
Separates results into actionable categories
Read-only: modifies nothing
Tells the user how to apply updates (/plugin for plugins, the skills installer for standalone skills)

evals.name: standard-improve-research
evals.prompt: My installed 'research' skill feels dated. Give it a standard cleanup pass to improve its structure and quality.
evals.expected_output: An improved COPY of the research skill plus a proposal explaining each change; description rewritten for triggering; structural/progressive-disclosure improvements; identity preserved; live skill untouched.
assertions: Delivers an improved copy; does not edit the live skill in place
Rewrites description for triggering with concrete when-to-use situations
Preserves skill name and core purpose
Applies a structural / progressive-disclosure improvement, not just cosmetics
Every file referenced from the improved SKILL.md actually exists in the copy and is wired to it (no dangling references)
Proposal explains reasoning per change tied to a found weakness

evals.name: deep-improve-deck-builder
evals.prompt: Make my 'deck-builder' skill best-in-class. Really research it — web, current docs, comparable skills — and bring it up to the state of the art.
evals.expected_output: An improved COPY of deck-builder plus a research-backed proposal citing web/Context7/skills-market/GitHub findings, translating them into concrete edits; verifies tool currency (pandoc/PPTX); marks research provenance when live fetching is degraded; identity preserved; live skill untouched.
assertions: Delivers an improved copy; does not edit the live skill in place
Performs external research across at least two distinct channels (web search, Context7 docs, skills marketplace, GitHub) with named sources and concrete cited findings
Verifies currency of dependencies (pandoc / PPTX behaviour)
Translates findings into concrete edits, not a link list
Applied code changes compile/parse, and the proposal's claimed change set matches the actual diff against the original (no phantom or unreported edits)
Research findings are marked with provenance: which were fetched live this run vs recalled from prior knowledge, explicitly declaring any research track whose tools were unavailable or blocked
Proposal justifies each change with reasoning/source
Preserves skill identity and core purpose

evals.name: seed-lessons-loop
evals.prompt: We keep re-learning the same mistakes in this repo. Set it up so the project actually gets better from them on its own — using what went wrong in this session as the starting evidence.
evals.expected_output: A lessons loop installed into the project — queue, archive, SessionStart hook, graph checker, capture skill and drain skill, adapted to the project's directory conventions — with the queue populated from mistakes visible in the session transcript, the hook registered in .claude/settings.json, the checker demonstrated firing against a seeded oscillation and 2x recurrence, and both skills wired into checkpoints that already fire.
assertions: Installs all six artefacts (queue, archive, SessionStart hook, graph checker, capture skill, drain skill), adapting paths to the project's existing docs/scripts/tests directory names
Registers the SessionStart hook in .claude/settings.json without clobbering hooks or settings already there

Demonstrates the checker firing: runs it against a fixture holding a deliberate oscillation and a 2x recurrence, shows the full reversal chain and the MOVE IT verdict, and shows a non-zero exit — rather than asserting it works
Triggers the SessionStart hook and shows the context it actually injects

Populates the queue from mistakes visible in the session transcript, each with What happened (including how it was caught), a Generalises to written as a followable rule, and a Candidate home marked as a suggestion
Does not implement or route any queue entry during seeding — routing is deferred to the drain

Wires both skills into checkpoints that already fire (a definition of done and a decision-settled moment), amending existing ones rather than inventing a parallel ceremony, and registers the two documents in the project's docs index
Detects an existing installation and offers an upgrade that preserves the archive and queue, rather than overwriting them
Both installed skill descriptions trigger on symptoms rather than on the phrase 'lessons learned'
The archive's own fenced format example is not reported as data by the hook or the checker
